Robert Murray M'Cheyne
ROB-urt MUR-ee muh-KAYN
proper noun (person)
Scottish minister (1813-1843) of St Peter's, Dundee, known for personal holiness and a widely used Bible reading plan; dead at twenty-nine.

📖 Biblical Definition

Robert Murray M'Cheyne was a Scottish minister of the Church of Scotland, pastor of St Peter's in Dundee, whose brief life of twenty-nine years left a lasting mark through the beauty of his personal holiness and the tenderness of his Christ-centered ministry. He labored amid a season of revival, preaching with affection and earnestness, and was so marked by communion with God that his very presence was said to convict. After his early death of typhus, his friend Andrew Bonar published the Memoir and Remains of Robert Murray M'Cheyne, which became one of the most influential devotional books in the English-speaking church, spreading his example of holiness far beyond his short life. M'Cheyne is also remembered for his Bible reading calendar, a plan that leads the believer through the whole Bible in a year, the New Testament and Psalms twice — still widely used today. His often-quoted conviction, that "the greatest need of my people is my personal holiness," captures his ministry. M'Cheyne stands in the dictionary as a pattern of pastoral holiness and a guide to the daily reading of Scripture, who taught the church that the minister's first work is to be a holy man, and that the daily, systematic reading of the whole Word is the food of the believing soul.

Scottish minister (1813-1843) of St Peter's, Dundee, dead at twenty-nine; a pattern of pastoral holiness whose Memoir (by Andrew Bonar) and whole-Bible reading plan have fed the church ever since.

ROBERT MURRAY M'CHEYNE, proper noun. Scottish minister (1813-1843) of St Peter's, Dundee.

Marked by deep personal holiness and Christ-centered, affectionate preaching.

Labored amid a season of revival; died of typhus at twenty-nine.

Subject of the Memoir and Remains by Andrew Bonar.

Author of a widely used calendar for reading through the whole Bible in a year.

📖 Key Scripture

1 Tim 4:16 — "Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee."

Psa 1:2 — "But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night."

1 Tim 4:12 — "Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity."

Josh 1:8 — "This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

M'Cheyne's life honors the recovery of personal holiness as the heart of ministry and the daily, systematic reading of the whole Bible, against a professionalized ministry that prizes skill over sanctity and a piecemeal reading that neglects the whole counsel of God.

expand to see more

Gifts-over-holiness correction. The modern church often prizes a minister's talent, charisma, and skill above his sanctity. M'Cheyne's conviction cuts the other way: "the greatest need of my people is my personal holiness." The dictionary holds with the apostle, "Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine" (1 Tim 4:16); the man is the message, and no eloquence can substitute for a holy life. M'Cheyne's example recalls every servant of God to the priority of personal godliness.

This entry faces little postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the daily, systematic reading of the whole Word. M'Cheyne's calendar leads the believer through all of Scripture in a year, refusing to leave any part neglected. The dictionary commends the discipline, fitting for a ministry like this one devoted to the reading of the Bible: the soul is fed by delighting in the law of the LORD and meditating in it day and night (Psa 1:2), and the whole counsel of God, read in order, is the believer's daily bread.
